title: Module contract, tool modules and presets
objective: Finish the module contract so a new tool is a declaration plus its equations: declared source kinds, one presettable-action rule, field patches over the whole parameter vocabulary with structural invariants, a descriptor snapshot instead of hand-kept lists, a smaller ToolModule and descriptor, developer-only test modules, and the shared Exposure and White balance controls once the owner answers their open questions.
context_summary: The consolidation made Basic, the colour mixer, Presence and the vignette one field-patch module each, gave the host layer identity, format and mask, and one placement rule. What remains: applicability to a source kind is decided by the RAW module's name in six places even though the declaration itself is already decided; field patches take numbers only, so the developer controls proof is a second patch implementation and Tone Curve could not be expressed as a spec; field-patch specs restate their invariants by hand; four hard-coded lists of built-in modules must be edited for every new module; and the trait, descriptor and test suites carry mechanisms with only one user. The owner's decisions are in docs/decisions.md's "Post-consolidation review" section; constraints are in docs/design/post-consolidation.md.

tasks.description: Replace the preset importer's false "Luxforge has no masks" message and correct the presets design doc's stale masking and catalog-format passages.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. Masking is delivered, so telling an importing user Luxforge has no masks is a false statement about current behavior, not a scope note.

`presets/mapping.rs`'s `NO_MASKS` constant reads "Luxforge has no masks or local corrections" and is reported for every imported Lightroom mask row; `presets/tests.rs` asserts that exact text. `docs/design/presets.md` repeats "Luxforge has no such tool" for the same row, and separately says "The current format is 7" with the format's branch history, while the catalog's own format marker is 10.

Reword the reason to something like "Lightroom masks and local corrections are not imported" (mask presets stay out of scope by decision; only the wording is wrong). Point the format passage at its one authoritative home instead of restating the number or its history.
No behavior changes: the importer still refuses Lightroom mask settings, only the message and the doc text change.

tasks.description: Declare each effect's source-kind applicability on EffectDescriptor and resolve "does this apply to this photo" through one function used by action refusal, admission, module.list and the desktop.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. Declared source kinds remove the desktop's name checks in the same change.

The rule "RAW applies only to a RAW photo" is written six times today: `api/methods.rs`'s `module_list` filters the literal `"luxforge.raw"`, but only when the request carries an `asset_id`; the desktop's own call to it (`app/tasks.rs`'s `modules_task`) sends none, so the desktop's own checks are what actually enforce this there. `editor/source.rs`'s `validate_source_recipe` names `crate::RAW_EFFECT` directly on its JPEG branch. The desktop repeats `module.id != "luxforge.raw"` (or the mode-string form) in `app/mod.rs`, `state/tools.rs`, `state/canvas.rs` (whose own comment calls this "the one thing the descriptor cannot say") and `state/palette.rs`.

Owner decision: a module's applicability to a source kind is declared, not named by the desktop. This is part 1 of the source-kind design and touches none of that design's open questions, so it lands on its own.

Current shapes only: EffectDescriptor gaining a `sources` field is an additive schema change. The RAW-only invariants that stay separate (one source layer at index zero, calibration equal to the asset's) are not part of this rule and are untouched.
The rendered raw-panel check needs a private RAW manifest; without one, verification is limited to the JPEG smoke scenarios and the desktop's unit and state tests.

tasks.description: Generalize the field-patch module's Field and Values to any declared parameter kind, and turn the developer controls proof into a field-patch spec so every patch control shares one semantics.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. Tone Curve, the next planned module, needs this to be a spec rather than a third hand-written module.

`field_patch.rs`'s Field holds only f64 state and Values holds a Vec<f64>, so its `read` re-implements the numeric range check `check_value` already provides, and its labels format numbers only. `tests/modules/conformance/shape.rs`'s `Field::read` accepts only Number parameters, so a curve, enum or boolean patch module is invisible to the suite.

`modules/controls.rs` (281 lines, the only exerciser of curve, toggle, choice and colour patch controls) hand-writes merge, canonical form, a no-op test by JSON-map equality (so a stored `{"amount":1}` and the bare number `1.0` count as different), and "exactly one field" enforced twice, and it refuses a stored default that equals the field's own declared default.

The curve control vocabulary stays even though only the controls proof uses it today; Tone Curve is its planned consumer, so the generalization must leave curve, enum, boolean and colour controls usable by a real module, not only the proof.

Renders stay byte-identical: every numeric module must keep compiling the same f64s through the generalized accessor. A stored-payload refusal's wording may change under current-shapes-only, but the conformance suite's refusal-by-name checks must still pass.

tasks.description: Implement the shared Exposure and White balance control set for JPEG and RAW photos per the source-controls design, once the owner has answered its open questions.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation.

Blocked on the owner's answers to the design's open questions: where Exposure lives on RAW, masked white balance on RAW, the JPEG and RAW scales and ranges, Lightroom RAW temperature and tint import, presets across source kinds, and whether Reset Basic also returns RAW white balance to As shot. Declared source kinds land independently of those questions, ahead of this work.

The host still reads the RAW module's payload directly: editor/source.rs's raw_settings, resolve_raw_settings, development_gains and raw_payload all parse RawPayload, and resolve_raw_settings and development_gains each resolve its white-balance mode to gains with the same As-shot/Custom match, written a third time inside the module itself. The payload's capture calibration (as_shot_gains, cam_xyz) is stored in every entry and re-compared against the asset's own at admission. Let the RAW module compile its own payload into a host source-development value instead, and take calibration from the stage context the way sensor_neutral already does.

Without a field patch that accepts every declared parameter kind, a patched set-raw would be a third hand-written patch semantics alongside the field patch and the developer controls proof. StageContext also carries no source kind today, so the RAW module's plan inspects the stack's first layer directly instead of being told the kind; give it one as part of this work.

A query also carries no mask target, so a masked Neutral picker would resolve against the stage before the global Basic layer applies, which is wrong whenever a global white balance exists; the desktop avoids this today only by leaving mask mode before entering Basic's pick mode. Resolve this rather than leaving it latent.

RAW action identities and payload fields are hard-coded in the harness (xtask/src/raw_editor.rs's script steps and control checks, xtask/src/raw_panel_smoke.rs's constants and field lookups); these move to the merged action and its fields with this change.

tasks.description: Build the vignette's per-row and per-column falloff tables lazily on first use instead of in the unit's constructor, and measure owner-thread time per slider tick with a shaped vignette at 60 MP.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed.

modules/vignette/unit.rs's Vignette::new builds two Vec<f64> tables sized width and height (15,840 entries combined at 60 MP, 9504x6336) with a powf call per entry whenever roundness is negative (the superellipse branch), and it runs at every compile, not only at render; vignette/mod.rs's compile constructs a fresh Vignette on every call.

The registry's compile_layers_sampled (modules/registry/compile.rs, which imports render::{Compiled, Entry, Segment, spatial} directly) also runs for callers that need only the output stage: editor/plan.rs's with_stage_context (every plan, draft.set, a composite step and a query), editor/evaluate.rs's analysis_identity (once per preview job), and editor/describe.rs through input_stages.

Suspected cost: roughly +0.1 to +1.5 ms of owner-thread time per slider tick on any module when the stack holds a superellipse vignette (two to three compiles per tick, plus one per preset step), against the draft.set round-trip p50 of about 0.2-0.3 ms recorded in docs/specs/performance.md.
Renders and the vignette's describe and is_finite outputs must stay byte-identical; this is a lazy-build change only, not a change to the falloff arithmetic.

tasks.description: Trim ToolModule to one describe hook in place of three always-together methods, collapse to one history-label mechanism, stop parse re-validating already-declared ranges, and remove the always-unreachable Unavailable forwarding wrapper.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure.

modules/mod.rs's ToolModule trait has 11 methods. describe_layer, values and is_neutral are always read together, by editor/describe.rs and registry/compile.rs's layer_neutral, each re-reading the same payload; collapsing them into one describe(...) -> LayerReport removes about 60 lines across the 8 implementations and the wrapper.

Two label mechanisms coexist: label() (used by the field patch and presets) and declared summary templates (used by pixel.rs, crop/module.rs and transform.rs, with their own machinery in descriptor.rs), combined at one site in editor/plan.rs; the desktop never reads summary.

parse in crop/module.rs, pixel.rs and modules/raw.rs re-checks ranges and enum membership the generic parameter check already enforces (raw.rs's own wording includes "missing EV" and "missing Kelvin"), about 80 lines of a second validation vocabulary. The Unavailable wrapper in registry/mod.rs forwards all 11 methods, but every host path checks availability first (plan.rs's available(), compile.rs through provider(), describe.rs, the capability host), so only its parse forward in a composite step is ever reached.

Owner decision: label() with the action's title as its default replaces summary templates; every stored history label stays byte-equal. This changes the mechanism, not the outcome, of the earlier decision to declare summary templates.

tasks.description: Delete the prebuilt JSON-descriptor parse path, give each Control variant its own struct so a wrong builder call is a compile error, add EffectDescriptor and ActionDescriptor constructors, and split descriptor.rs by concern.

AGENTS.md rules out building for external module loading now ("required later, not now"), so deleting the JSON-parse path removes dead generality rather than a used capability. tasks.description: Delete the per-module copies of sample-equals-render, the host-journey re-run, neutral-compiles-to-nothing and compile-refusal checks that the shape-driven conformance suite now proves generically, naming each deleted assertion's keeper.
extra_context: Wave 5, tests.

Per-module copies of host-level checks remain after the registry-driven conformance suite took them over: sample-equals-render in tests/basic/{exposure,white_balance,tone,colour}.rs, tests/modules/{mixer,presence}.rs and xtask/src/basic_acceptance.rs; the host journey re-run in tests/basic/exposure.rs; "neutral compiles to nothing" in modules/basic/mod.rs, modules/mixer/mod.rs, modules/presence/mod.rs and presence/oracle.rs; compile refusals in basic/mod.rs; and discovery checks in vignette/mod.rs and tests/basic/white_balance.rs.

The per-module Presence sampling alone is the most expensive part of the modules test binary: tests/modules/presence.rs runs 2 images times 4 parameter sets times 1,280 pixels times 2 render paths, about 26 million pixel evaluations, to prove what the render-level spatial suite already proves with cheap units.

Keep each module's numerics against its own frozen corpus, its history-word tests, its placement test and any genuinely module-specific behavior. Add the field-order assertions the deleted per-module tests incidentally provided for the mixer and vignette (one describe-based assertion each), so a field-order swap is still caught. A commit that deletes a test names, for each assertion, the kept test that proves the same fact.

Separately, replace the private re-implementations of the sRGB transfer function scattered across roughly 15 test files (three different, mutually disagreeing definitions under the same few names, including inside the reference crate's own studies) with calls to one named set of functions the reference crate exports.

tasks.description: Give ToolModule a defaulted carry hook so a later geometry module is repositioned by the orientation the way the crop is today, instead of transform.rs naming the crop directly.
extra_context: Wave 6, roadmap groundwork.
Blocked: starts when the first new geometry module (for example upright or perspective) is designed.

modules/transform.rs imports crop::stored_payload and CROP_EFFECT directly and re-expresses only the crop through a turn, via CropPayload's carried method in modules/crop/geometry.rs — the one piece of module-to-module coupling anywhere in modules/. A second geometry effect placed after the orientation (an upright or perspective module, say) would keep its stored payload unchanged while its input stage turns, so it would silently address different image content; nothing today refuses this.

Non-affine geometry is out of scope for the hook itself: it would need a new host primitive through processing.rs, registry/compile.rs's output_stage, render.rs's point walk, render/pipeline.rs, render/linear.rs, render/window.rs and render's locate path. Record that in docs/design/architecture.md so a future module does not fake one through the carry hook.
